Driven by large language models, AI agents are transforming drug discovery, enabling AI to break free from task-specific tools and advance toward the vision of autonomous virtual scientists. This perspective reviews applications across the R&D lifecycle. To evaluate system maturity, we introduce a 6-level “Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy.” We advocate for novel evaluation paradigms centered on full-chain traceability and outline adoption barriers, positioning AI agents as pragmatic scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.
. Research strategies that rely predominantly on iterative trial-and-error experimentation are increasingly inadequate for navigating the scale and complexity of modern chemical and genomic spaces
. As a result, the pharmaceutical industry faces growing pressure to adopt new paradigms that move beyond incremental efficiency gains and instead provide mechanistic insight and predictive power capable of reducing late-stage failure. Driven by this practical demand, computational methods in drug discovery have continuously evolved, gradually transitioning from experience-driven auxiliary tools to a technological foundation capable of participating in core decision-making
